correctness.rationale: The real Hilbert–Schmidt dissipation identity forces peripheral eigenoperators to commute with each positively weighted rank-one projector. They are block diagonal with diagonal even block C. The commutator with the hopping Hamiltonian is off-diagonal, excluding nonzero imaginary eigenvalues. At zero, the two hopping block equations give [C,TT†]=0; off-diagonal entries of TT† at distance two connect the even words, forcing C scalar (automatic for d=1). The odd block differs from the same scalar by an arbitrary operator supported on ker T on both sides. Norm contraction excludes a Jordan block at zero. The adjoint generator reverses the Hamiltonian sign and has the same kernel, so the limiting spectral projection is indeed Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal, giving the stated all-state formula including dark coherences. Complementary Walsh zero modes pair to give one odd-supported mode per pair in even d, and none in odd d. Even translations make the odd-site dark weight constant, so its square yields the 2/(πd) term by Stirling; the bright term is exponentially small. A direct d=2 check gives T all ones, rank(D)=1, odd-site return 1/3. The uploaded numerical checker was inspected, not run; the exact limit and asymptotic are proved analytically and do not establish a relaxation rate uniform in d.

value.rationale: The explicit full limit distinguishes dark coherence retention from ordinary mixing, and predicts an order-1/d return where an exponentially small return might be expected on 2^d vertices. It also settles all initial states and arbitrary positive site strengths in the specified model without relying on uniform rates. This is informative without any claim about relaxation time.
